cause_1: Cracked hose coupling on the cooling water manifold
cause_2: Loose or failed hose clamp at the manifold connection
cause_3: Leaking seal or O-ring in the mould cooling circuit
steps:
Isolate the water supply and lock out the machine
Dry the area before touching any electrical parts
Cut out and replace the cracked coupling (new hose coupling and clamp)
Check the rest of the manifold for other cracks
Restore water and check for leaks
Do not just tape the coupling or mop and ignore it
safety_warnings: Lock out the machine; dry the wet floor and area before touching electrical parts; slippery floor/fluid spill hazard

cause_1: Clogged filter in the spindle chiller circuit
cause_2: Low or wrong coolant in the spindle chiller circuit (restricted flow)
cause_3: Chiller pump or flow fault
steps:
LOTO the machine
Drain the chiller reservoir
Remove and clean the chiller filter
Refill with the correct spindle coolant
Run for 30 minutes and confirm the temperature stays under the limit; check alarm ALM-410 is clear
Bearings are probably fine (log shows swapped bearings did not help)
safety_warnings: LOTO before work; electrical energy hazard; let the hot spindle housing cool before touching

cause_1: Worn piston seal letting oil pass inside the cylinder
cause_2: Relief valve stuck partly open from contamination
cause_3: Leaking holding/check valve on the cylinder line
steps:
Support the ram with safety blocks
LOTO and bleed down/depressurise the press
Remove the cylinder head
Replace the piston seals and check the bore
Reassemble and run a hold test for ten minutes
safety_warnings: Stored hydraulic pressure; support the ram with safety blocks before working; LOTO and depressurise

cause_1: Unmelted plastic frozen in the barrel after a cold start
cause_2: Failed thermocouple or heater band so part of the barrel never reaches temperature
cause_3: Screw drive/motor fault (less likely; swapped motors were fine in the log)
steps:
Do NOT pull the nozzle off while the barrel is at temperature
LOTO the screw drive
Bring the barrel up to temp and heat soak for the full soak time
Retry screw rotation at low torque (do not force it with higher torque)
Purge the barrel with purging compound
Verify the melt temperature is stable
safety_warnings: Hot barrel and molten plastic burn hazard; do not remove the nozzle hot; wear face shield and heat-resistant gloves; forcing the screw can shear it

cause_1: Worn and loose drive belt
cause_2: Misaligned or glazed pulleys
cause_3: Worn motor or pump bearings
steps:
Stop and lock out the compressor
Remove the belt guard
Check belt wear and tension
Replace the belt and re-tension (tension gauge)
Refit the guard and test
Do not spray belt dressing on the running belt
safety_warnings: LOTO; rotating pulley/belt hazard; never spray dressing on a running belt; refit guard before restart

cause_1: Carbonised material trapped in a dead spot in the barrel and hot runner
cause_2: Contaminated or undried material (check dryer settings)
cause_3: Failed thermocouple causing a barrel temperature fault
steps:
Lock out and make the area safe from molten material
Purge the barrel with purging compound
Clean the nozzle and hot runner tip
Dry the material and check the dryer settings
Run parts and check for specks
Lowering barrel temperature or changing masterbatch does not fix it
safety_warnings: Hot barrel/molten plastic; LOTO; wear face shield and heat-resistant gloves

cause_1: Seized idler roller dragging on the belt
cause_2: Worn lagging on the drive pulley (squeal on start)
cause_3: Failed roller bearing with no grease
steps:
Stop, LOTO and wait for drive discharge
Spin the idler rollers by hand to find the seized one
Replace the seized roller and bearing
Inspect drive pulley lagging and check belt tension against spec
Check belt and drive current
Restart and confirm no overcurrent trip
Do not raise the VFD current limit or swap the VFD (drive was not at fault)
safety_warnings: LOTO and wait for drive discharge; moving belt/rollers; do not spray lubricant on a running roller

cause_1: Cracked hose coupling on the cooling water manifold (the leak)
cause_2: Worn check ring letting melt flow back (parts not filling)
cause_3: Insufficient shot size or material feed
steps:
Treat as two faults; do not just mop the floor
Water leak: isolate water, lock out, dry area, replace cracked coupling, check manifold, restore water and check for leaks
Filling: lock out and let the barrel cool to a safe temperature, pull the screw, inspect check ring and seat
Replace the worn check ring set, reinstall and confirm a steady cushion
Do not raise injection pressure or shot size
safety_warnings: LOTO; dry area before touching electrical parts; slippery floor; let barrel cool before pulling the screw

cause_1: Faulty pressure switch so the compressor never unloads
cause_2: Safety valve itself faulty or set too low
cause_3: Unloader/inlet valve stuck so the compressor keeps building pressure
steps:
Do NOT wedge, plug or fit a higher-rated safety valve
Stop and lock out the compressor
Vent to zero pressure
Test the pressure switch against a calibrated gauge
Replace the faulty pressure switch
Restart and confirm it unloads at cut-out
safety_warnings: Safety valve is the overpressure protection; blocking it is extremely dangerous; LOTO and vent to zero before work; electrical energy

cause_1: Air drawn into the circuit through a loose suction fitting
cause_2: Low oil level in the tank letting the pump draw air
cause_3: Relief valve stuck partly open from contamination
steps:
LOTO and bleed down the press
Inspect all suction side fittings and hoses
Tighten or replace the leaking suction fitting (and hose clamp)
Bleed air from the circuit at the cylinder bleed points
Run cycles until motion is smooth
Changing only the oil or replacing the proportional valve will not fix it
safety_warnings: High-pressure fluid injection hazard; LOTO and depressurise before touching fittings

cause_1: Clogged pump suction strainer
cause_2: Relief valve stuck partly open from contamination
cause_3: Air drawn in through a loose suction fitting
steps:
LOTO and bleed down the press
Drain the tank to the strainer level
Remove and clean the suction strainer
Refill with filtered hydraulic oil
Run empty cycles and time the ram
Do not replace the pump (it was cavitating from the blocked strainer)
safety_warnings: LOTO and bleed down; hot oil / hot surfaces

cause_1: Encoder cable chafed in the drag chain
cause_2: Loose or damaged encoder connector
cause_3: Faulty encoder or electrical noise on the signal
steps:
LOTO and wait for drive discharge
Inspect the encoder cable along the drag chain
Replace the chafed cable section, or re-route and clip it clear of the chain edge
Power up and confirm a stable speed reading
Do not just clear the alarm or replace the spindle drive
safety_warnings: LOTO and wait for drive discharge before touching cables

cause_1: Blocked automatic drain valve on receiver
cause_2: Air dryer fault/ineffective moisture removal
cause_3: not sure
steps: Stop and lock out compressor; vent receiver to zero pressure; clean or replace automatic drain valve; manually drain receiver and check for rust; restart and verify drain cycles.
safety_warnings: Isolate and depressurise fully before opening drain/receiver components; beware stored compressed air and slippery water/oil spills.

cause_1: Worn check ring allowing melt to flow back
cause_2: not sure
cause_3: not sure
steps: Lock out machine and allow barrel to cool to a safe temperature; pull screw; inspect check ring and seat; replace worn check ring set; reinstall and confirm steady cushion position.
safety_warnings: Lock out; allow barrel to cool fully; protect against hot barrel/molten plastic; use appropriate screw-pulling tools.

cause_1: Water ingress and corroded terminals in pull-cord switch
cause_2: Damaged switch seal allowing moisture ingress
cause_3: not sure
steps: Lock out and prove dead; inspect pull-cord switch and terminals; replace corroded terminals and switch seal; test the e-stop circuit end to end; obtain supervisor sign-off before returning to production.
safety_warnings: Do not bypass or defeat the emergency-stop circuit; isolate and prove dead; verify the complete safety circuit and obtain supervisor sign-off.

cause_1: Pitted contactor contacts causing phase imbalance
cause_2: Loose or burned power terminal causing single-phasing
cause_3: not sure
steps: Lock out and prove dead; open starter cabinet; inspect contactor and terminals; replace pitted contactor; check motor current on all three phases; restart and confirm overload remains closed.
safety_warnings: Electrical isolation and prove-dead required; account for residual capacitor/drive voltage; work only by qualified personnel.

cause_1: Encoder cable chafed in drag chain
cause_2: not sure
cause_3: not sure
steps: Do not work with power on. Stop and isolate the machine; wait for drive discharge; inspect encoder cable along drag chain; replace damaged cable section or reroute and secure it clear of chain edges; power up and confirm stable spindle-speed reading.
safety_warnings: Never work on live electrical/drive equipment; LOTO and wait for drive discharge before inspection or repair.

cause_1: Faulty pressure switch causing compressor not to unload
cause_2: Blocked automatic drain valve on receiver causing water/rust in pipework
cause_3: not sure
steps: Stop and lock out compressor; vent receiver to zero pressure; test pressure switch against a calibrated gauge; replace faulty pressure switch; clean or replace automatic drain valve; manually drain receiver and inspect for rust; restart and confirm unloading and drain operation.
safety_warnings: Never plug, disable or obstruct the safety valve; depressurise to zero before opening components; preserve overpressure protection; electrical isolation required.

cause_1: Failed oil separator element
cause_2: not sure
cause_3: not sure
steps: Stop and lock out compressor; vent to zero pressure; allow oil to cool; remove separator cover and old element; fit new separator element; top up compressor oil; restart and check operation.
safety_warnings: Isolate and fully depressurise before opening; allow hot oil to cool; observe electrical safety.

cause_1: Light curtain misaligned and lenses dirty
cause_2: not sure
cause_3: not sure
steps: Lock out the press; clean emitter and receiver lenses; realign light curtain using alignment indicators; run and record the safety-function test; obtain supervisor sign-off before returning to production.
safety_warnings: Do not bypass or defeat the light curtain; keep the press out of service until safety function is tested, recorded and signed off.

cause_1: Failed roller bearing with no grease
cause_2: not sure
cause_3: not sure
steps: Stop and lock out conveyor; identify squealing roller by spinning it by hand only after isolation; replace failed bearing; grease all bearings to schedule; restart and listen for abnormal noise.
safety_warnings: Do not adjust, lubricate or work near a moving conveyor; isolate and lock out; beware moving belt/rollers and crush or pinch points.

cause_1: Blocked air intake filter
cause_2: not sure
cause_3: not sure
steps: Stop and lock out compressor; vent receiver to zero pressure; remove and inspect intake filter; replace filter element if blocked; restart and check pressure build-up time.
safety_warnings: Isolate equipment and vent stored compressed air to zero before opening; beware electrical energy.

cause_1: Starved X-axis ball screw due to clogged way-lube line
cause_2: Turret not fully clamped because chips are packed under clamp face
cause_3: not sure
steps: Stop machine, lock out and wait for drive discharge; trace way-lube line to X-axis ball screw; clear blocked line and replace clogged metering block; run lube pump manually until oil appears; jog axis and confirm load drops. Separately, inspect turret clamp face for packed chips, clean it, verify seating with feeler gauge and run a test cut if chatter persists.
safety_warnings: Lock out and wait for drive discharge before axis work; beware residual capacitor/drive voltage; never reach into moving machinery.

cause_1: Unmelted plastic frozen in barrel after cold start
cause_2: not sure
cause_3: not sure
steps: Lock out screw drive; bring barrel up to operating temperature and heat-soak for the full required time; retry screw rotation at low torque; purge barrel with purging compound; verify melt temperature is stable.
safety_warnings: Do not force the screw with higher torque; it can shear the screw. Beware hot barrel and molten plastic; use face shield and heat-resistant gloves.

cause_1: Worn seal in the rotary hydraulic union leaking pressure
cause_2: Leaking pilot-operated check valve on the chuck clamping line
cause_3: Faulty hydraulic pressure switch or external line leak
steps:
Stop the spindle and LOTO
Depressurise the chuck hydraulic line and verify zero pressure
Remove the rotary union cover
Replace the worn union seal kit
Re-pressurise and test clamping with a scrap part
safety_warnings: Watch out for rotating spindle / chuck / pulley and stored hydraulic pressure

cause_1: Stretched drive chain
cause_2: Worn or hooked sprocket teeth
cause_3: Sprocket misalignment or seized chain links
steps:
Stop and LOTO the conveyor
Measure the chain elongation
Replace the stretched chain
Check sprocket tooth wear and alignment
Re-tension to spec and lubricate
safety_warnings: Watch out for moving belt / chain / rollers and pinch points

cause_1: Build-up on an idler roller pushing the belt off line
cause_2: Idler or tail roller misaligned / not square to the frame
cause_3: Off-center material loading or worn pulley lagging
steps:
Stop and LOTO the conveyor
Find the idler roller with material build-up
Clean the roller surface and check it spins freely
Square the roller to the frame
Restart and watch the belt track for a few minutes
safety_warnings: Watch out for crush / pinch points and moving rollers

cause_1: Unmelted plastic frozen in the barrel after a cold start
cause_2: Carbonised material trapped in a dead spot in the barrel and hot runner
cause_3: Failed thermocouple or heater band causing localized overheating and cold slugs
steps:
LOTO the screw drive and ensure the area is safe from molten material
Bring the barrel up to temperature and heat soak for the full soak time
Retry screw rotation at low torque
Purge the barrel with purging compound
Clean the nozzle and hot runner tip
Dry the material, check dryer settings, and run parts to inspect for specks
safety_warnings: Watch out for hot barrel / molten plastic; wear face shield and heat-resistant gloves

cause_1: Leaking minimum pressure check valve
cause_2: Faulty pressure switch or narrow cut-in/cut-out differential
cause_3: Blocked receiver drain reducing air buffer capacity
steps:
Stop and LOTO the compressor
Vent the receiver to zero pressure
Remove the check valve and inspect the seat
Replace the faulty check valve or seal
Restart and watch the load/unload cycle
safety_warnings: Watch out for stored compressed air and electrical energy

cause_1: Stretched drive chain jumping sprocket teeth (over-tightening tensioner added drag)
cause_2: Seized idler roller dragging on the belt
cause_3: Damaged drive/gearbox bearing from over-tensioning
steps:
Stop, LOTO, and wait for VFD drive discharge
Measure chain elongation and replace the stretched chain and worn sprockets
Spin the idler rollers and drive shaft by hand to check for seized bearings
Re-tension chain to spec, check belt and drive current, and restart without overcurrent trip
safety_warnings: Watch out for residual capacitor / drive voltage and moving chain/rollers

cause_1: Worn rod seal damaged by a scored cylinder rod
cause_2: Degraded rod wiper seal
cause_3: Loose or damaged cylinder gland
steps:
Refuse working under an unsupported ram: always support the ram with mechanical safety blocks first
LOTO and bleed down / depressurise the press
Remove the gland and old rod seal
Polish minor rod scoring or replace the rod if deep
Fit a new rod seal and wiper and test for leaks
safety_warnings: Never work under a hydraulic ram without mechanical safety blocks; watch out for suspended/gravity load and stored hydraulic pressure

cause_1: Debris on the mould parting line
cause_2: Damaged mould shut-off surfaces
cause_3: Insufficient clamping tonnage or excessive injection pressure
steps:
Refuse reaching in by hand without blocking/LOTO: never reach in while platens can move
Stop the machine, LOTO, and make sure the mould is cool
Open the mould and clean the parting faces with brass tools and mould cleaner
Inspect for damaged shut-off surfaces
Apply mould protector, close slowly, and run a test shot
safety_warnings: Never reach into the mould area while platens can move; watch out for crush/pinch points and hot barrel/molten plastic

cause_1: Suction strainer packed with swarf
cause_2: Low coolant level causing pump air-lock
cause_3: Clogged coolant line/nozzle or failed pump impeller
steps:
LOTO the machine
Remove the coolant tank cover
Lift out and clean the suction strainer
Refill coolant (suds) to the mark and bleed the pump
Restart and check coolant flow at the nozzle
safety_warnings: Watch out for sharp swarf / hot chips, slippery fluid spills, and electrical energy

cause_1: Fouled cooler fins restricting airflow
cause_2: Blocked air intake filter
cause_3: Incorrect cooling fan direction or stuck thermostatic bypass valve
steps:
Stop and LOTO the compressor
Let the compressor cool down
Clean the cooler fins with low-pressure air from the clean side
Check the cooling fan direction and inspect the air intake filter
Restart and monitor discharge temperature
safety_warnings: Watch out for electrical energy and hot surfaces/oil

cause_1: Loose or burned power terminal causing single-phasing
cause_2: Pitted contactor contacts causing phase imbalance
cause_3: Failed unloader/check valve forcing start under pressure or seized pump bearings
steps:
Stop and LOTO the compressor and prove dead
Inspect motor and starter cabinet terminals and contactor contacts
Tighten loose connections or replace burned terminals/contactor
Check unloader valve operation and verify balanced current on all three phases under load
safety_warnings: Watch out for electrical energy and residual voltage before opening starter cabinet

cause_1: A part stuck in the cavity from the previous cycle
cause_2: Debris or misaligned ejector/core pin obstructing mould closure
cause_3: Faulty platen position transducer or low-pressure mould protection timeout
steps:
Stop the machine and LOTO
Never reach in while the platens can move
Remove the stuck part using brass tools
Inspect mould faces for damage
Reset and cycle slowly with mould protection on
safety_warnings: Never reach in while platens can move; watch out for crush / pinch points and suspended gravity load

cause_1: Damaged tool setter probe giving bad offset readings
cause_2: Worn cutting insert
cause_3: Loose turret clamp or thermal growth
steps:
Stop the machine safely
Test the tool setter probe against a known gauge pin
Replace the damaged probe tip
Recalibrate tool offsets
Run a five-part check to confirm sizes
safety_warnings: Stop the spindle and make the machine safe before reaching near the tool setter or chuck.

cause_1: Seized idler roller dragging on the belt (causing load fault)
cause_2: Water ingress and corroded terminals in the pull cord e-stop switch
cause_3: Loose wiring or faulty safety relay
steps:
Stop, lock out (LOTO) the conveyor, and wait for drive discharge
Spin the idler rollers by hand to find any seized roller and replace the roller and bearing
Open the pull cord switch box, dry it out, and replace corroded terminals and the switch seal
Test the e-stop circuit end to end and check belt and drive current
Get supervisor sign-off before returning to production
safety_warnings: LOTO and prove dead before opening the pull cord switch box, and wait for VFD capacitor discharge before working on rollers.

cause_1: Worn lagging on the drive pulley
cause_2: Low belt tension
cause_3: Seized roller or jammed belt
steps:
Stop and lock out (LOTO) the conveyor
Inspect the drive pulley lagging
Re-lag or replace the worn pulley lagging
Check and set belt tension against the spec
Run a loaded test
safety_warnings: Lock out the conveyor before working near the drive pulley or belt nip points.

cause_1: Failed roller bearing with no grease
cause_2: Debris wrapped around the roller shaft
cause_3: Misaligned or bent roller
steps:
Stop and lock out (LOTO) the conveyor
Confirm the bad roller by spinning by hand
Remove and replace the failed roller bearing
Grease all bearings to schedule
Restart the conveyor and listen for smooth running
safety_warnings: Never spray lubricant onto a running conveyor; lock out first to avoid moving belt and roller pinch points.

cause_1: Dirty and slightly misaligned photo-eye (affected by afternoon sunlight/glare)
cause_2: Failed roller bearing with no grease
cause_3: Loose sensor bracket or damaged reflector
steps:
Stop and lock out (LOTO) the conveyor
Clean the photo-eye sensor lens and reflector, then realign them and verify the signal on diagnostics
Spin the rollers by hand to locate the squealing roller and replace the failed bearing
Grease all bearings to schedule
Restart and watch several cycles
safety_warnings: Lock out the conveyor before cleaning/realigning sensors or replacing bearings near moving belts and rollers.

cause_1: Seized idler roller dragging on the belt
cause_2: Belt overloaded or jammed with product
cause_3: Drive motor or gearbox binding
steps:
Stop, lock out (LOTO) the conveyor, and wait for drive discharge
Spin the idler rollers by hand to find the seized roller
Replace the seized roller and bearing
Check belt tracking and drive motor current
Restart and confirm there is no overcurrent trip
safety_warnings: LOTO and wait for residual VFD capacitor discharge; watch for moving belt and roller pinch points.

cause_1: Starved ball screw because the way-lube line is clogged
cause_2: Clogged lube metering block
cause_3: Low way-lube oil level or failed lube pump
steps:
Lock out (LOTO) the lathe and wait for drive discharge
Trace the way-lube line to the X-axis ball screw
Clear the blocked lube line and replace the clogged metering block
Run the lube pump manually until oil appears at the screw
Jog the X axis and confirm the servo load drops
safety_warnings: LOTO and wait for residual capacitor/drive voltage discharge before accessing axis covers.

cause_1: Seized idler roller dragging on the belt
cause_2: Belt jammed or overloaded
cause_3: Drive gearbox or motor fault
steps:
Do not work on the conveyor with power on — stop, lock out (LOTO), and wait for drive discharge first
Spin the idler rollers by hand to find the seized one
Replace the seized roller and bearing
Check belt and drive current with a clamp meter
Restart and confirm no overcurrent trip
safety_warnings: UNSAFE REQUEST REFUSED: Working on a conveyor with power on risks severe entanglement in moving belts/rollers and electric shock from drive voltage. Full LOTO and drive discharge are mandatory.

cause_1: Debris on the mould parting line
cause_2: Damaged shut-off surfaces on the mould
cause_3: Excessive injection pressure or low clamp tonnage
steps:
Lock out (LOTO) the machine and let the mould cool
Open the mould and clean the parting faces with a brass scraper and mould cleaner
Inspect the shut-off surfaces for damage
Apply mould protector and close the mould slowly
Run a test shot to confirm flash is gone
safety_warnings: LOTO before reaching between platens; watch for hot mould surfaces, molten plastic, and crush/pinch points.

cause_1: Dry ejector guide pins with no lubrication
cause_2: Worn or galling ejector bushes
cause_3: Bent ejector pin
steps:
Lock out (LOTO) the moulding machine
Open the mould and pull the ejector plate
Clean and inspect the guide pins and bushes
Apply the correct high-temp mould grease
Cycle the ejector by hand to confirm smooth travel
safety_warnings: LOTO the machine before opening the mould; watch for crush/pinch points around the ejector plate.

cause_1: Blocked automatic drain valve on the air receiver
cause_2: Clogged moisture separator or air dryer drain
cause_3: High ambient humidity with heavy condensate load
steps:
Do not open any valve or fitting under pressure — stop and lock out (LOTO) the compressor first
Vent the air receiver completely to zero pressure and verify on the gauge
Clean or replace the blocked automatic drain valve
Manually drain the receiver and check for internal rust
Restart the compressor and verify the auto drain cycles properly
safety_warnings: UNSAFE REQUEST REFUSED: Never open a receiver or drain valve without venting to zero pressure first; stored compressed air can violently eject parts and cause serious injury.

cause_1: Failed thermocouple reading low so the heater stays on continuously
cause_2: Welded or stuck solid-state relay / heater contactor
cause_3: Loose thermocouple probe not seated properly in the barrel
steps:
Switch off the heaters, lock out (LOTO) the machine, and let the barrel cool
Test the zone thermocouple against a reference thermometer
Replace the failed thermocouple
Power up and watch the zone heat to setpoint without overshoot
safety_warnings: Switch off heaters, LOTO for electrical safety, and allow the hot barrel and smoking plastic to cool before working.

cause_1: cracked hose coupling on the cooling water manifold
steps:
isolate the water supply and lock out the machine
dry the area before touching electrical parts
cut out and replace the cracked coupling
check the manifold for other cracks
restore water and check for leaks
safety_warnings: wet floor is a slip hazard; dry the area before touching electrical parts

cause_1: clogged filter in the spindle chiller circuit
steps:
lock out the machine
drain the chiller reservoir
remove and clean the chiller filter
refill with the correct coolant
run for 30 minutes and make sure the temp stays under limit
safety_warnings: spindle housing too hot to touch, let it cool before opening the chiller circuit

cause_1: worn piston seal letting oil pass inside the cylinder
steps:
support the ram with safety blocks
lock out and bleed down the press
remove the cylinder head
swap out the piston seals and check the bore
reassemble and run a hold test for ten minutes
safety_warnings: stored hydraulic pressure; support the ram with safety blocks before bleeding down

cause_1: unmelted plastic frozen in the barrel after a cold start
steps:
lock out the screw drive
bring the barrel up to temperature and heat soak for the full soak time
retry screw rotation at low torque
purge the barrel with a purging compound
verify the melt temperature is stable
safety_warnings: do not open or pull the nozzle while the barrel is at temperature; hot barrel / molten plastic can burn you. wear a face shield and heat-resistant gloves

cause_1: worn and loose drive belt
steps:
stop and lock out the compressor
remove the belt guard
check belt wear and tension
swap out the belt and re-tension
refit the guard and test
safety_warnings: never spray belt dressing on a running belt, unsafe near rotating parts and only a temporary fix

cause_1: carbonised material trapped in a dead spot in the barrel and hot runner
steps:
lock out the machine and make sure the area is safe from molten material
purge the barrel with purging compound
clean the nozzle and hot runner tip
dry the material and check the dryer settings
run parts and inspect for specks
safety_warnings: hot barrel / molten plastic; wear a face shield

cause_1: worn lagging on the drive pulley
cause_2: seized idler roller dragging on the belt
steps:
stop and lock out the conveyor
inspect the drive pulley lagging
re-lag or replace the pulley lagging
check belt tension against the spec
spin the idler rollers by hand to check for a seized one
test run loaded and make sure no overcurrent trip
safety_warnings: watch for the moving belt / chain / rollers

cause_1: cracked hose coupling on the cooling water manifold
cause_2: worn check ring letting melt flow back
steps:
isolate the water supply and lock out the machine
dry the area before touching electrical parts
cut out and replace the cracked coupling
check the manifold for other cracks
restore water and check for leaks
if parts still do not fill, lock out and let the barrel cool, pull the screw and inspect the check ring and seat
safety_warnings: wet floor near electrics is dangerous; dry before touching electrical parts; hot barrel / molten plastic when checking the check ring

cause_1: faulty pressure switch so the compressor never unloads
steps:
stop and lock out the compressor
vent the receiver to zero pressure
test the pressure switch against a calibrated gauge
swap out the faulty pressure switch
restart and confirm it unloads at cut-out
safety_warnings: never wedge or plug a safety valve, it removes overpressure protection and is extremely dangerous; also stored compressed air in the receiver

cause_1: air drawn into the circuit through a loose suction fitting
steps:
lock out and bleed down the press
inspect all suction side fittings and hoses
tighten or swap out the leaking suction fitting
bleed air from the circuit at the cylinder bleed points
run cycles until motion is smooth
safety_warnings: watch out for high-pressure fluid injection when opening fittings

cause_1: clogged pump suction strainer
steps:
lock out and bleed down the press
drain the tank to the strainer level
remove and clean the suction strainer
refill with filtered oil
run empty cycles and time the ram
safety_warnings: stored hydraulic pressure; watch for hot oil

cause_1: encoder cable chafed in the drag chain
steps:
lock out and wait for drive discharge
inspect the encoder cable along the drag chain
replace the chafed cable section and clip it clear of the chain edge
power up and confirm a stable speed reading
safety_warnings: wait for drive discharge before opening the cabinet; residual capacitor / drive voltage
